title: Variable-turn fairness batcher with KV hinting and GPU slab shims
creator: Lena Chen
description: We see tail latency regressions for workloads with interleaved short prompts and long responses. Current continuous batching favors throughput and ends up starving short-turn interactive traffic or over-reserving KV residency for long-turns, increasing GPU memory pressure and forcing slab compaction more often. This ticket implements a fairness-aware continuous-batcher variant that uses light-weight per-turn hints to guide KV reservation and soft slot preemption ("kv hinting"), plus GPU slab shims to reduce fragmentation. Goals: reduce P95 latency for short-turn interactive traffic by ~20% without increasing overall cost-per-token by >5% and avoid additional OOMs/compactions.
acceptance_criteria: P95 latency for interactive short-turn traffic decreases by >=18% on the mixed benchmark compared to baseline continuous-batcher
Overall token throughput remains within 5% of baseline for the mixed benchmark
Number of slab compaction events per hour reduces or stays flat compared to baseline
No increase in customer-facing 5xx errors during canary rollout
Automated regression tests added for mixed-turn microbenchmarks and KV hint path
proposed_solution: Introduce a fairness layer in the continuous batcher that tracks per-request 'turn-length-hint' metadata. Use hints to: 1) place requests into short/long soft-queues with proportional slot admission; 2) apply KV hinting to tag cache entries as 'ephemeral' vs 'resident' and prefer ephemeral eviction for predicted short-turns; 3) enable soft preemption where long-turn slots yield to short-turns when latency SLOs are at risk. Add a GPU slab shim allocator that groups ephemeral KV allocations into compactable pools to reduce fragmentation and speed up compaction. Implement feature flags and telemetry for each subcomponent so we can toggle preemption, kv-hinting, and slab-shim independently during canarying.
implementation_notes: Add 'turn_length_hint' optional proto field in request metadata; default behaviour unchanged if absent
Batcher: implement an admission controller that enforces a short-turn target ratio per time-slice and uses token-aware admission scoring
KV cache: add lightweight hint bit on cache entries and eviction policy extension to prefer hinted evictions
GPU allocator: introduce ephemeral slab arena with higher compaction frequency and memory headroom bookkeeping
Instrumentation: per-request trace ids, queue wait times, kv residency duration histogram, slab fragmentation metric (largest-free-chunk / total-free), compaction duration
Backwards compatibility: requests without hints follow existing flow and will be treated conservatively as 'long' to avoid evicting useful entries
test_plan: Unit tests for admission controller scoring and quota enforcement
KV cache unit tests for hinted evictions and TTL semantics
E2E microbench: synthetic mix with 60% short prompts (<8 tokens) and 40% long responses (>512 tokens), measure P50/P95/P99 latency and compaction events
Chaos test: induce a GPU memory spike and validate graceful degradation path and fallback to baseline model variant
Integration test in staging against dedicated pool with 4 x A100 to measure slab fragmentation changes
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged deployment: enable kv-hinting only (no preemption/allocator) in Canary A (1% traffic) for 48h
If stable, enable short/long admission controller in Canary B (5% traffic) for 48h
Enable slab-shim allocator in a small dedicated cluster behind a canary routing rule; monitor compaction latency and OOMs for 72h
Full rollout across mixed-traffic pools with staggered enablement and automated rollback triggers on P95 regressions or increased 5xx
Post-rollout: 2-week observation window with daily reports to SRE and capacity planning
risks: Incorrect turn-length hints from SDKs could misclassify long-turns as short and cause quality regressions due to premature eviction
Soft preemption may increase retransmits if preempted long-turns have to restart or rehydrate KV state
Slab-shim allocator changes could reveal latent fragmentation bugs leading to higher OOM frequency in edge clusters
Monitoring noise early in rollout may cause false rollbacks; need stable baselines before canary expansion
